basics.description: Access Review portal in your existing virtual network. The web app, PostgreSQL and Key Vault get private endpoints and have no public access. The template creates no virtual network and no subnets. Choose the region of your virtual network.

location.label: Region
location.toolTip: The region of your virtual network. All resources and private endpoints are created in this region.

options.text: Before you start: the app registration (client ID and secret), a subnet for App Service and a subnet for private endpoints in your virtual network, and the DNS plan for the private endpoints. Select this box to open the guide.

Choose your virtual network and two of its subnets. The template creates no virtual network and no subnets. The list shows the virtual networks in the region above, in all subscriptions that you can read.

elements.name: vnet
elements.label: Virtual network
elements.toolTip: The virtual network with the two subnets. It must be in the region above.

elements.name: appSubnet
elements.label: App Service subnet
elements.toolTip: VNet integration of the web app: all its outbound traffic goes through this subnet. The list shows the subnets that are delegated to Microsoft.Web/serverFarms. /28 or larger, /26 recommended.

options.text: This virtual network has no subnet delegated to Microsoft.Web/serverFarms. Ask your network team to delegate an empty subnet (/27 or /26): Subnets > the subnet > Subnet delegation > Microsoft.Web/serverFarms. The subnet is then only for App Service.

elements.name: endpointSubnet
elements.label: Private endpoint subnet
elements.toolTip: The private endpoints of the web app, PostgreSQL and Key Vault (three IP addresses). The list shows subnets without delegation.

constraints.allowedValues: [map(filter(coalesce(basics('network').vnetApi.properties.subnets, parse('[]')), (s) => and(not(contains(parse('["GatewaySubnet","AzureFirewallSubnet","AzureFirewallManagementSubnet","AzureBastionSubnet","RouteServerSubnet"]'), s.name)), empty(s.properties.delegations))), (s) => parse(concat('{"label":"', s.name, ' (', coalesce(s.properties.addressPrefix, ''), ')","value":"', s.id, '"}')))]

options.text: Choose two different subnets. The App Service subnet is only for App Service.

basics.name: appName
basics.label: App name
basics.toolTip: Name of the web app. The portal address is https://<App name>.azurewebsites.net. Must be unique in Azure.

validations.message: 2-58 characters: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens. No hyphen at the start or the end.

basics.name: appServicePlanSku
basics.label: App Service plan size
basics.toolTip: P0v3 is enough for most tenants. See docs/SIZING.md.

basics.name: clientId
basics.label: Client ID
basics.toolTip: Application (client) ID of the app registration of the portal.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter the GUID of the application (client) ID.

basics.name: clientSecret
basics.toolTip: Value of a client secret of the app registration. The template stores it in Key Vault.

elements.name: databaseServer
elements.label: Database server
elements.toolTip: Azure Database for PostgreSQL: the template creates the server with a private endpoint. Your own server: for example PostgreSQL on a VM; the template creates no server.

elements.name: databaseAuthentication
elements.label: Sign-in to PostgreSQL
elements.toolTip: Managed identity: the identity id-<App name> of the web app is the Microsoft Entra administrator of the server. The server accepts no passwords.

elements.name: postgresAdminPassword
elements.toolTip: Password of the administrator login accessreviewadmin. The template stores the connection string in Key Vault.

elements.name: postgresServerName
elements.label: Server name
elements.toolTip: Name of the PostgreSQL server. Must be unique in Azure. Empty: psql-<App name>.

constraints.validationMessage: 3-63 characters: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens.

elements.name: postgresSize
elements.label: Compute size
elements.toolTip: Burstable B2s is enough for most tenants. See docs/SIZING.md. The size must be available for your subscription in the region.

options.text: Prepare your server first: a login that owns the database accessreview, TLS, a pg_hba.conf line for the address range of the App Service subnet, and port 5432 open from this subnet.

elements.name: existingServerConnectionString
elements.toolTip: Example: Host=pg01.contoso.com;Port=5432;Database=accessreview;Username=accessreview;Password=<password>;Ssl Mode=VerifyFull. The template stores it in Key Vault.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter an Npgsql connection string, for example Host=pg01.contoso.com;Port=5432;Database=accessreview;Username=accessreview;Password=<password>;Ssl Mode=VerifyFull

elements.name: existingServerCaCertificate
elements.label: CA certificate (optional)
elements.toolTip: Only when the server certificate comes from your own CA: the CA certificate as base64 of the .cer file, or PEM. Needed for Ssl Mode=VerifyFull.

elements.name: dnsMode
elements.label: Private DNS zones
elements.toolTip: New zones: the template creates privatelink.azurewebsites.net, privatelink.postgres.database.azure.com and privatelink.vaultcore.azure.net in the resource group and links them to the virtual network. Existing zones: your central zones, for example in a hub subscription.

options.text: [concat('This virtual network uses custom DNS servers (', string(basics('network').vnetApi.properties.dhcpOptions.dnsServers), '). New zones in this resource group are linked only to this virtual network, so these DNS servers do not see them. Use the existing zones that your DNS servers resolve.')]

Users open the portal from your network. Your DNS must resolve <App name>.azurewebsites.net to the private endpoint, for example with a conditional forwarder for privatelink.azurewebsites.net to an Azure DNS resolver.

body.query: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.network/privatednszones' and name in~ ('privatelink.azurewebsites.net', 'privatelink.postgres.database.azure.com', 'privatelink.vaultcore.azure.net') | join kind=leftouter (resourcecontainers | where type =~ 'microsoft.resources/subscriptions' | project subscriptionId, subscriptionName = name) on subscriptionId | project id, name, resourceGroup, subscription = coalesce(subscriptionName, subscriptionId) | order by subscription asc, resourceGroup asc

elements.name: siteZone
elements.label: Zone privatelink.azurewebsites.net
elements.toolTip: The zones with this name in the subscriptions that you can read: resource group (subscription).

constraints.allowedValues: [map(filter(coalesce(steps('dns').zonesApi.data, parse('[]')), (z) => equals(toLower(z.name), 'privatelink.azurewebsites.net')), (z) => parse(concat('{"label":"', z.resourceGroup, ' (', z.subscription, ')","value":"', z.id, '"}')))]

options.text: No zone privatelink.azurewebsites.net found in the subscriptions that you can read. Choose Create new zones, or ask for Reader on the zone.

elements.name: postgresZone
elements.label: Zone privatelink.postgres.database.azure.com
elements.toolTip: The zones with this name in the subscriptions that you can read: resource group (subscription).

constraints.allowedValues: [map(filter(coalesce(steps('dns').zonesApi.data, parse('[]')), (z) => equals(toLower(z.name), 'privatelink.postgres.database.azure.com')), (z) => parse(concat('{"label":"', z.resourceGroup, ' (', z.subscription, ')","value":"', z.id, '"}')))]

options.text: No zone privatelink.postgres.database.azure.com found in the subscriptions that you can read. Choose Create new zones, or ask for Reader on the zone.

elements.name: vaultZone
elements.label: Zone privatelink.vaultcore.azure.net
elements.toolTip: The zones with this name in the subscriptions that you can read: resource group (subscription).

constraints.allowedValues: [map(filter(coalesce(steps('dns').zonesApi.data, parse('[]')), (z) => equals(toLower(z.name), 'privatelink.vaultcore.azure.net')), (z) => parse(concat('{"label":"', z.resourceGroup, ' (', z.subscription, ')","value":"', z.id, '"}')))]

options.text: No zone privatelink.vaultcore.azure.net found in the subscriptions that you can read. Choose Create new zones, or ask for Reader on the zone.
Key Vault keeps the client secret and the database connection string. It has a private endpoint and no public access. The web app reads it with its managed identity.

elements.name: keyVaultName
elements.label: Key Vault name
elements.placeholder: Empty: a name derived from the resource group and the app name
elements.toolTip: 3-24 characters, unique in Azure. Empty: kv-<unique string>.

constraints.validationMessage: 3-24 characters: letters, digits and hyphens. Starts with a letter.

elements.name: enablePurgeProtection
elements.label: Purge protection
elements.toolTip: With purge protection, a deleted vault and its name stay reserved for 90 days. Recommended for production.
